chunks: When the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, returned to al-Madinah from the battle of Uhud, he heard lamentation and weeping from every house from whose people someone had been killed. But he did not hear from the house of Hamzah, his paternal uncle, so he said, peace be upon him and his family:

So the people of al-Madinah swore that they would not lament over any deceased nor weep over him until they began with Hamzah, lamenting over him and weeping for him; and they remain upon that to this day.

key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: al-Madinah, where the event took place after the battle
key_terms.بَوَاكِيَ: female mourners or those who weep in mourning

ai.seo_question: Why did the people of al-Madinah begin mourning for Hamzah before their own dead after Uhud?
ai.summary: This report describes the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله observing the mourning in al-Madinah after Uhud and noting the absence of mourners for Hamzah. In response, the people of al-Madinah adopted the practice of beginning mourning with Hamzah before mourning their own dead, showing his honored place and the community’s attachment to him.
